items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Jumbo Jackson was one. And, uh, Satchel Page was down here.

ctx.x: Well, those are the baseball teams in the days that I'm talking about. They're both Crescent Starks Park, and that's where the main, uh, baseball games were played, even when they brought the, uh, the big stars down, like the Chicago Giants. And, of course, they picked up a few of the ball players from around here. Jumbo Jackson was one. And, uh, Satchel Page was down here. He's pitched down here. And the great catcher, Josh Gibson, and all the guys that they're naming today, which is, uh, late in life they've…
You said you were in the studio, you told him. Right.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: Jumbo Jackson was a great player baseman.

ctx.x: I never have known. I know they had a team at one time called the Black Pelicans.

Well, that's why they named it. The Black Pelicans only called the Pelicans. Did you ever play with them? I never played. I was a boy. I was about eight, nine, eight or ten years old, possibly. You saw the Black Pelicans? Yes. I used to go to the Pelican, there's many catches, and sometimes the names come back to me. And Satchel Paige was down many times. And the team from Chicago, the Chicago Giants, used to take the players from the Orleans. They had one name. Jumbo Jackson was a great player baseman. And Hot…
And who else? You never saw Shooters Joe Jackson.
